辣子鸡

Lazi Chicken · Sichuan Chili Chicken

Prompt

Premium Chinese restaurant food poster featuring deconstructed layers of 辣子鸡 / Lazi Chicken / Sichuan Chili Chicken floating in a vertical stack on pure black background. Seven distinct layers from top to bottom, including a large empty gap before the finished dish. Upper layers are RAW, UNCOOKED recipe ingredients; only the final dish at the bottom is cooked.

1) Top layer: a small floating cloud of dry, unheated reddish-brown Sichuan peppercorns and pale ivory untoasted sesame seeds. Reveal the peppercorn husks and tiny seed textures.

2) Second layer: abundant vivid red dried chilies, some whole and some cut into short sections with a few visible seeds. These dried chilies are uncooked, with natural wrinkled skins, not fried or charred.

3) Third layer: fresh RAW bite-size chicken pieces, a mixture of small skin-on bone-in chunks and thigh pieces. Clearly show moist pale pink flesh, pale ivory skin and clean cut edges. Plain and unseasoned: no golden crust, orange sauce, breading, cooked browning or steam. Keep the pieces small enough for a classic Sichuan chili chicken dish, not whole drumsticks.

4) Fourth layer: crisp raw ginger slices, ivory sliced garlic and fresh green scallion segments, floating as a separate aromatic cluster. No sauteing, frying or browning.

5) Fifth layer: a transparent glass bowl containing clear, light straw-colored neutral cooking oil before heating. Smooth reflective surface, no chili infusion, no finished sauce, no frying bubbles and no steam.

6) Sixth layer: EMPTY SPACE - a generous gap with a few peppercorns, sesame seeds and fine spice particles drifting through it. Steam rises here only from the finished bowl below.

7) Bottom/Final layer: a complete cooked 辣子鸡 / Lazi Chicken in a dark brown ceramic bowl. Many crisp golden-brown bite-size fried chicken pieces are nestled among a generous mound of deep red stir-fried dried chili sections, Sichuan peppercorns, garlic, ginger and green scallion segments, lightly sprinkled with sesame seeds. Show crunchy browned chicken texture and a light appetizing oil sheen. This is a dry Sichuan stir-fry: no broth, curry gravy, thick wet sauce, potatoes, noodles or coconut milk. A subtle wisp of steam rises from the cooked bowl.

Chinese and English annotation pairs, in ingredient order:
"花椒与芝麻" / "Sichuan Pepper & Sesame"
"干辣椒" / "Dried Chilies"
"生鸡肉" / "Raw Chicken"
"姜蒜与葱" / "Ginger, Garlic & Scallions"
"食用油" / "Cooking Oil"
"成品" / "Finished Dish"

Each of the five ingredient layers floats freely with normal spacing. After the fifth layer, leave an intentional empty transition space two to three times larger than an ordinary gap. At the bottom, reveal the complete cooked dish in a traditional dark brown ceramic bowl. Use the same 45-degree camera angle and consistent scale and dramatic studio lighting throughout. All upper ingredient layers must look RAW or UNCOOKED AS USED BEFORE THIS RECIPE IS COOKED: plain pink meat, fresh crisp vegetables, unheated condiments and spices, and uncooked noodles where specified. No cooked crust, browned meat, stir-fried vegetables, finished meat sauce, or steam in the upper layers. Fermented pastes and tofu are shown as recipe ingredients before pan cooking.

Set everything against pure black (#000000), with warm rim lighting, realistic glass reflections, rich food textures, luxurious commercial restaurant photography and a 9:16 portrait format. Keep the ingredients centered. Place legible warm cream bilingual labels around them, alternating left and right, with thin elegant curved arrows. Chinese appears above English; render only the specified labels, once each, with generous margins and no overlap with food. The empty transition gap has no label. Only the finished dish emits subtle steam, rising into the transition gap. Add a few drifting spice particles appropriate to this dish and a small star sparkle at the bottom right beside the finished bowl. All layers float freely: no table, pedestal, platform, plate under the ingredients, extra title, logo, slogan or unrelated food.
